audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer phases[N].side read "Ekko" while content win[] read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Hwei/Hwei, and the whys under those Ekko rows described Hwei winning the stage.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches content win[] exactly, and 50.99% over 1969 games is an even lane. The kit reason: Phase Dive is 325 units and Z-Drive Resonance needs three hits on the same target, so Ekko has to come to Hwei before 6.
audit.corrected: phases[0..2].side = Hwei, phases[3..4].side = Skill, phases[5..6].side = Hwei, with the four affected whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[5] said both champions scale similarly off the first item on a row the chart awards to Hwei. Chronobreak's cooldown curve — the single biggest power shift in this matchup — appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 but 50s at rank 3. A page that tells the reader to "commit on Chronobreak's cooldown" without that number teaches the wrong instinct at 16.
audit.corrected: whys[5] now names the range reason for the row; the 110s/50s curve appears in breakdown.cooldowns, phases[4].why and dosFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never stated the one thing that decides the trade: Parallel Convergence only stuns if EKKO enters the anomaly himself. It also called Hwei's tools "EE fear", "EQ root" and "W root/charm", none of which exist.
audit.why: Riot's text: "If Ekko enters the anomaly, he gains shielding and stuns enemies by suspending them in time." The anomaly is placed from 1600 units and forms after a few seconds, so the counterplay is to leave the circle before he arrives — the stun is conditional on his own movement, not on yours. Hwei's E sub-abilities are Grim Visage / Gaze of the Abyss / Crushing Maw (EQ/EW/EE); his W paints are Fleeting Current / Pool of Reflection / Stirring Lights.
audit.corrected: Leave the circle and he gets neither the shield nor the stun. Grim Visage (EQ) is held for Phase Dive landing, which reaches only 325 units.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four flagged interactions were absent: Chronobreak's untargetability, its heal (anti-heal timing), Parallel Convergence's shield, and Phase Dive's auto-attack reset as the burst tell.
audit.why: missingInteractions lists all four for this matchup. Chronobreak makes him untargetable, rewinds him, and heals a percentage of damage received in that window — so burst spent into it is spent twice over.
audit.corrected: Hold the killing paint until he reappears; buy anti-heal before you try again; force the shield out; step back on the Phase Dive wind-up, not on the cast. Added across cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d, feeding, loading, late and wants.you[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED); breakdown.cooldowns had no digit.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles; cooldowns now carries Chronobreak 110s/50s, Parallel Convergence 22s and Phase Dive 9s/325 units.

audit.why: packet.suspectNames flags "Drive Resonance", "Use Chronobreak" and "Ekko's Parallel Convergence" as probable wrong names. All three are false positives — the names match packet.enemyAbilities exactly and the matcher is tripping on the surrounding words.
audit.corrected: No name changes made on that basis.

notes: Chart: all seven full-layer sides read "Ekko" against content win[] of Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Skill/Hwei/Hwei, with Hwei-favoured whys sitting underneath the Ekko rows. Sides now match content and packet.levelChart; win[] needed no edit. Ratings left at 7/7/7/7/8/7/7. The interaction the page never stated: Parallel Convergence stuns only if EKKO enters the anomaly — the counterplay is to leave the circle, not to dodge a projectile. All four of the flagged missing interactions (untargetable, heal/anti-heal, shield, auto-reset tell) are now on the page. Also worth the user's attention: Chronobreak drops from 110s to 50s at rank 3, and the page's repeated "commit on Chronobreak's cooldown" advice was being given without that number, which teaches an over-confident window late. packet.suspectNames flagged three ability names here; all three are false positives matching packet.enemyAbilities exactly. Did NOT assert whether Grim Visage or Hwei's R can be dodged by Chronobreak's untargetability window in a way that refunds the cast, or whether the anomaly blocks anything — neither is in the kit text.
